content.value_statement: Unclear skills can cause agents to skip guidance or follow weak instructions. This skill helps authors create, test, refine, and verify reusable AI skills for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Defines when a skill should be created or avoided.
Explains frontmatter, naming, and Claude Search Optimization rules.
Shows how to test skills with pressure scenarios and subagents.
Provides a deployment checklist for skill creation and revision.
Includes Anthropic skill authoring best practices as reference material.
Includes a Graphviz helper for rendering skill flowcharts.
limitations: Requires an existing understanding of test-driven development.
Does not create skills automatically without human review.
Graph rendering needs Graphviz installed and trusted local skill files.
Examples are focused on Claude-style skill workflows.

use_cases.title: Create a New Skill
use_cases.description: Plan, draft, and verify a reusable skill before adding it to an agent library.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Guidance
use_cases.description: Find weak descriptions, missing tests, and unclear instructions in an existing skill.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether a skill has evidence, tests, examples, and deployment steps before publication.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Skill Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: decide whether a new skill is justified.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this task pattern and tell me whether it deserves a reusable skill. Explain the trigger conditions and reasons to avoid creating one.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Skill Frontmatter
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft the name and description for a skill about this workflow. Keep the description focused only on when the skill should be used.

prompt_templates.title: Design Pressure Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify behavior under realistic pressure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three pressure scenarios that test whether an agent follows this skill under time pressure, authority pressure, and sunk cost.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor After Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: improve a skill after failed verification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these failed test transcripts. Identify the rationalizations, revise the skill guidance, and list the exact checks needed before deployment.

output_examples.input: A draft skill description explains the full workflow in one paragraph.
output_examples.output: The revised description states only the trigger conditions. The workflow details move into the skill body where the agent must read them.

output_examples.input: An agent skipped TDD because the task felt urgent.
output_examples.output: The review identifies time pressure as the failure mode and adds a pressure scenario that forces an explicit choice before implementation.

output_examples.input: A skill contains long reference material and a reusable helper script.
output_examples.output: The structure keeps core guidance in the main file and moves heavy reference or reusable tooling into supporting files.

best_practices: Run a baseline pressure test before writing or changing the skill.
Keep the frontmatter description focused on when to use the skill.
Use supporting files only for large references, reusable tools, or examples.
anti_patterns: Writing a skill because one session solved a one-off problem.
Putting workflow summaries in descriptions that let agents skip the full skill.
Adding untested instructions and assuming agents will follow them under pressure.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you author, revise, test, or review AI skills for agent workflows.

faq.question: Does it write the skill for me?
faq.answer: It provides structure, tests, and review guidance. A human still reviews the final skill.

faq.question: Why does it require baseline testing?
faq.answer: Baseline testing shows how agents fail without the skill, so the guidance can target real failure modes.

faq.question: Can it help with existing skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify weak descriptions, missing pressure tests, and unclear deployment steps.

faq.question: Does it require extra tools?
faq.answer: Most guidance is markdown. The optional flowchart renderer requires Graphviz and a local script.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, though many examples use Claude skill paths.
